setter.evidence: No setter named. The prospect self-describes as inbound off the founder's content — 'I follow the guy that I signed up from. So I've been following him for a long time.'

prospect.name: Jess
prospect.training_background: Weight trains in cycles — 'I do weight training, and I go to get in shape, and I go for about a month or two, and then I'll end up injuring myself, and then I need to sit out, and then I'm out for, like, a month.' Has used kettlebells before but never a full kettlebell system. Has followed the founder's content for around two years.
prospect.medical: Recurring training injuries — 'I get injured every time I work out' and 'I got injured, so I'm tired of getting injured.' Nature, site and severity of the injuries were never established; the rep did not ask.

signals: Wants a former self back — the rep reads back from the application, 'I said you wanted to get your athletic body back', and the prospect does not dispute it
Has lost ground repeatedly to injury rather than to inactivity — a month or two of progress wiped out by a month on the sidelines, on repeat
Low confidence assignment: the call was terminated at five minutes, so there is no age, occupation, income, family, deeper motive or history on file. The assignment rests on two lines.

goals.text: Get his athletic body back — stated by the rep from the application and not disputed
A more functional workout routine that does not keep injuring him
Break the injure-rest-restart cycle and be able to train continuously — 'I don't want to stop working and get injured. I want to be able to continue to work on it.'

pains.text: Gets injured roughly every one to two months of weight training and loses a month each time
Progress is repeatedly reset by the injury cycle — 'and then it's just like... A cycle, right?'
Distrusts how online fitness offers are sold — 'anything you buy online now, it seems to kind of go like this'

objections.rep_response: Confirmed it could run longer and immediately offered the exit — 'You don't need to do it if you don't want to' — which the prospect took: 'Yeah, I'm probably gonna pass, then.' The rep then challenged him with the application line rather than rebuilding the frame.

objections.raw_quote: I mean, I'm just, I'm just trying to figure out like what is this system or whatever, but like, I feel like if we're just going to do like a whole big sales pitch and the whole thing, like, I'm really not interested.
objections.rep_response: Defended the process and offered the exit a second time — 'I can give you the price, but eventually it's not going to be a good fit if we don't know if we can help you... again, if you don't want to do it, that's totally fine.' Never acknowledged the prior bad experiences, never separated this call from the ones he was reacting to.

evidence: The rep ended the call — 'It sounds like you don't want to have this conversation, but that's totally fine. If you don't want to, we can hang up right now.'
Sign-off was 'Sorry for the waste of time, bro.'

Counter-evidence that the prospect was still in it: he kept answering discovery questions for four minutes after saying he would pass, disclosed his injury cycle, his two years following the founder, and his motive — 'I got injured, so I'm tired of getting injured.'

In the review of this call the same day, the reviewing closer's read was that the prospect was interested throughout — 'he does give a [damn], there's just a little bit of skepticism' and 'this guy actually seemed pretty cool, dude.'
No price named, no offer presented, nothing collected, no follow-up arranged and no plan to call him back — 'I don't have time to call him.'
outcome.next_step: None. No follow-up was agreed on the call and none was arranged afterwards.

notable.note: Five-minute call terminated by the rep. It was reviewed the same day by the other closer, whose verdict was that it was lost in the first sixty seconds on rapport and energy rather than on fit — see 2026-07-06_richard-claessen-x-michael-brideau-call-review. The opening move was a comment on the prospect's posture ('Seems like you're a little bit laid out, is that correct?'), the exit was offered twice inside ninety seconds, and the prospect's stated reason for being there — a repeating injury cycle from weight training — was surfaced and then dropped without a single question about what the injuries actually are.

quality.notes: Mostly clean, with clear swaps where the rep's questions land under the prospect's label — 'You're doing some workouts but not working at some moments and you're injuring yourself, or...?' at 00:02:35 and 'A cycle, right?' at the same turn. Several of the prospect's answers are merged into the rep's blocks near the end. The prospect's display label is 'iPhone (3)'; his first name comes from the paired review call, where the reviewing closer asks 'what's this guy's name?' and is told 'Jess'. No surname was ever said.
